$comment: Every exception to a gate lives here, and every entry answers four questions:
what     -- the key: the exact token, script or path being excused
why      -- the reason, in a full sentence, readable by someone who was not there
who      -- the owner: who decided, and who to ask before removing it
expires  -- an ISO date after which the gate fails until someone renews it,
or "never", which is only allowed when `why` says why it is permanent
The expiry is the point. An allowlist without one is a decision that quietly becomes
policy: nobody revisits it, and in a year nobody can say whether it is still true.
scripts/check-allowlists.mjs enforces the shape and the dates; the guard-break suite
proves it fails when an entry expires.

xez-skill.why: Prose, not a skill reference: documents say "a new xez-skill" as a common noun. Permanent, because it is the collection's naming convention rather than an exception to it.

xez-skills.why: Prose, not a skill reference: documents say "the xez-skills collection". Permanent, because it is the collection's own name.

chaining-lines:skills/xez-issue-create/r.why: Files an issue and hands back; it emits no chaining reference line, so carrying the marker contract would cost always-loaded tokens for a rule it never applies. Permanent while the skill stays create-only.

chaining-lines:skills/xez-ux-review-pr/r.why: Reports UX findings as tracker comments; it never emits a chaining reference line of its own. Permanent while it neither opens nor drives a pull request.

chaining-lines:skills/xez-ux-setup/refer.why: Sets up UX tooling locally and emits no tracker artifact, so there is no chaining line to shape. Permanent while it stays a local setup skill.

chaining-lines:skills/xez-ux-shape/refer.why: Produces a design shape document, not a tracker artifact, so it emits no chaining reference line. Permanent while it stays document-only.

test:agent-browser-codex.why: Needs the `codex` CLI and a full-access sandbox. A CI runner has neither, and granting full access to a pull request's own code is exactly what CI must not do.
